# The generated YAML

What the app produces for [shared models](/guide/shared-models). You can
read the exact file before it is used: **Settings → Shared models** shows a
preview.

```yaml
# cpo:generated
# Generated by ComfyUI Portable Organizer. Manual edits will be overwritten.
cpo_shared_0:
  base_path: D:/AI/_shared_models
  is_default: true
  checkpoints: checkpoints/
  loras: loras/
  vae: vae/
  text_encoders: |
    text_encoders/
    clip/
  diffusion_models: |
    unet/
    diffusion_models/
  controlnet: controlnet/
  upscale_models: upscale_models/
  embeddings: embeddings/
```

## Why it looks like that

**`# cpo:generated` on the first line.** This is how the app recognises its
own file when it finds one in a build folder, so that it can rewrite its
own and refuse to touch yours. The marker is ASCII and does not change
between versions — recognition cannot depend on the human-readable line
below it, which can be translated or edited.

**`cpo_shared_<n>` as the section name.** ComfyUI iterates over the
top-level keys and does not care what they are called. A name of our own
means we never collide with a `comfyui:` section you wrote yourself.

**Forward slashes.** They work on Windows and need no escaping, unlike
backslashes in YAML.

**Absolute `base_path`.** Relative paths would be resolved against the
folder holding the YAML, which differs between the two apply modes. An
absolute path means the file behaves identically wherever it sits.

**Block scalars (`|`) for several folders.** ComfyUI splits a key's value
on newlines, so this is how one category gets both `unet/` and
`diffusion_models/`.

**`is_default`** follows the "Download new models here" switch. In ComfyUI
it decides whether the path goes to the front of the list for its
category — which is where newly downloaded files land. It does not affect
what is found.

## What is not in it

**`custom_nodes` is never generated**, under any circumstances, even when
the folder exists in your shared root. The key is valid and it appears in
ComfyUI's own example file, which is exactly why it is worth saying: nodes
shared between builds is the failure mode separate builds exist to avoid.

Subfolders the app does not recognise are not written either. They are
listed in the interface so you can see what was skipped and rename it if it
was a typo.

## The categories

Sections come from the subfolders that actually exist in your shared root —
the folder names *are* the keys. The app knows the categories that shipped
with ComfyUI 0.30 (`checkpoints`, `loras`, `vae`, `controlnet`,
`upscale_models`, `embeddings`, `clip_vision`, `style_models`, `gligen`,
`hypernetworks`, `photomaker`, `audio_encoders`, and so on) but only to
offer creating the missing ones and to flag typos.

Two legacy names are folded into their modern keys, the same way ComfyUI
does internally:

| Folder on disk | Key written |
| --- | --- |
| `unet/` | `diffusion_models` |
| `clip/` | `text_encoders` |

## Where the file goes

**Flag mode** — `%APPDATA%\io.github.quo0.comfyui-organizer\shared-models.yaml`,
handed over with `--extra-model-paths-config`. Nothing is written inside
your build.

**File inside the build** — `<build>\ComfyUI\extra_model_paths.yaml`. An
existing file that is not ours is backed up as
`extra_model_paths.yaml.bak-<timestamp>` and replaced only after you
confirm on a screen that shows both.

## Checking that ComfyUI took it

With the build running:

```
http://127.0.0.1:<port>/internal/folder_paths
```

Every category with the list of paths behind it. Your build's own paths are
still there — the shared ones are added, not substituted.
